items.description: The traditional lamidat of Banyo in the Adamawa region. It reflects the long-standing Muslim rule of the northern plateau.
The lamidat of Ngaoundere is a major traditional authority center in Adamawa. It remains a key symbol of local rule and heritage.
The palace of King Bell in Douala is tied to one of the city's best known ruling families. It preserves the memory of coastal leadership.
A bridge in Edea dating back to the German colonial period. It is one of the town's old engineering landmarks.
A traditional chiefdom in western Cameroon. It preserves the institutions and symbols of local Bamileke power.
The lamidat of Maroua is the traditional power center of the Far North capital. It reflects the region's Islamic political history.
The palace of King Akwa in Douala belongs to one of the city's influential royal families. It is an important part of Duala history.
Dschang's colonial center preserves traces of German and French administration. It is one of the city's most historic areas.
The lamidat of Garoua is a major traditional institution on the Benue River. It anchors the city's historical and social identity.
The old slave market site in Pitoa recalls historic trade routes in northern Cameroon. It stands as a difficult memorial site.
The name Rio dos Camaroes refers to the Portuguese naming of the Wouri estuary. It is part of the origin story of Cameroon itself.
The site of the old fort in Yaounde recalls the city's early colonial military outpost. It marks the start of its urban history.
A major Catholic cathedral in Douala. It is one of the city's most important religious buildings.
The old post office in Buea is a reminder of the town's colonial administrative era. It reflects the city's early public infrastructure.
The palace of Babungo is a traditional power center in northwest Cameroon. It preserves the history and rituals of the local court.
